knowledge:
- key_parameters: method=In fCNV() and aqtl(), specifies the association method; "spearman" uses correlation, while "mi" uses mutual information (which requires setting a seed for permutation reproducibility) ;; cores=In fCNV(), marina(), aqtl(), and conditional(), specifies the number of CPU cores for parallel processing (not supported on Windows for values > 1) ;; pheno=In marina() and conditional(), the name of the metadata column in the ExpressionSet containing sample phenotype labels ;; group1=In marina() and conditional(), the label for the test phenotype group (e.g., "MES") ;; group2=In marina() and conditional(), the label for the reference phenotype group (e.g., "PN") ;; mr=In aqtl() and conditional(), the Master Regulator gene(s) of interest to analyze ;; cnv=In conditional(), a threshold vector (typically 2.5% and 97.5% quantiles from normal samples) used to discretize continuous CNV data for Fisher's exact test ;; mindy=In aqtl(), a logical value; if TRUE, restricts the aQTL analysis to upstream post-translational modulators of the MRs as defined by the MINDy/CINDy interactome
- alternatives: Statistical models of genomic evolution (e.g., MutSigCV) or mutational bias can identify driver mutations based on frequency, but they require very large cohorts and do not provide mechanistic insights. Standalone Master Regulator activity can be inferred using the viper package.
- when_to_use: Use this workflow when you have matched gene expression and copy number variation (CNV) data for a cohort, along with a reconstructed transcriptional regulatory network (e.g., from ARACNe) and optionally a post-translational network (e.g., from MINDy), and you want to identify functional CNVs that drive a specific phenotypic transition by modulating Master Regulator activity.
- pitfalls: CNVs often span multiple genes, creating statistical dependencies similar to linkage disequilibrium. Failing to run conditional association analysis (conditional()) can lead to false-positive driver identifications that are merely passenger CNVs physically close to the true driver. Additionally, using method="mi" requires setting a random seed (e.g., RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG") and set.seed()) to ensure reproducible permutation-based p-values.

workflows.name: diggit_driver_inference
workflows.intent: Identify functional genetic drivers (CNVs) of a cellular phenotype by integrating expression, CNV, and regulatory networks.
input: gbmExprs (ExpressionSet containing gene expression data and phenotype metadata)
gbmCNV (Matrix of copy number variation data)
gbmCNVnormal (Matrix of copy number variation data from normal samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Initialize the diggit object using diggitClass ;; 2. Infer functional CNVs (fCNVs) associated with expression using fCNV ;; 3. Identify Master Regulators (MRs) of the phenotype using marina ;; 4. Map activity quantitative trait loci (aQTLs) linking fCNVs to MR activity using aqtl ;; 5. Perform conditional association analysis using conditional to filter out passenger CNVs in linkage disequilibrium ;; 6. Plot and summarize the conditional analysis results using plot and summary
workflows.code:
library(diggit)
data(gbm.expression, package="diggitdata")
data(gbm.cnv, package="diggitdata")
data(gbm.aracne, package="diggitdata")
data(gbm.mindy, package="diggitdata")
genes <- intersect(rownames(gbmExprs), rownames(gbmCNV))[1:1000]
gbmCNV <- gbmCNV[match(genes, rownames(gbmCNV)), ]
dobj <- diggitClass(expset=gbmExprs, cnv=gbmCNV, regulon=gbmTFregulon, mindy=gbmMindy)
dobj <- fCNV(dobj, method="spearman", verbose=FALSE)
RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG")
set.seed(1)
dobj <- fCNV(dobj, method="mi", cores=cores, verbose=FALSE)
dobj <- marina(dobj, pheno="subtype", group1="MES", group2="PN", cores=cores, verbose=FALSE)
dobj <- aqtl(dobj, mr=c("CEBPD", "STAT3"), method="mi", cores=cores, verbose=FALSE)
data(gbm.cnv.normal, package="diggitdata")
cnvthr <- quantile(as.vector(gbmCNVnormal), c(.025, .975), na.rm=TRUE)
dobj <- conditional(dobj, pheno="subtype", group1="MES", group2="PN", mr="STAT3", cnv=cnvthr, cores=cores, verbose=FALSE)
plot(dobj, "STAT3", cluster="2")
summary(dobj)
dobj <- aqtl(dobj, mr=c("CEBPD", "STAT3"), method="mi", mindy=TRUE, cores=cores, verbose=FALSE)
dobj <- conditional(dobj, pheno="subtype", group1="MES", group2="PN", mr="STAT3", cnv=cnvthr, verbose=FALSE)
summary(dobj)
